champion: Malignant solitary fibrous tumor of the spine
ordered_diagnoses: Malignant solitary fibrous tumor of the spine

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower back pain with radiating symptoms and evidence of a spinal lesion with potential metastatic disease
salient_findings: Lower back pain radiating to both groins for 2 months
Mixed sclerotic and lytic lesion in the T12 vertebral body
Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules and mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy
key_facts: 44-year-old man with no significant past medical history
Lower back pain radiating to both groins for 2 months
Normal vital signs
Unremarkable physical examination
Normal routine laboratory studies
Mixed sclerotic and lytic lesion in the T12 vertebral body on CT scan
Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules on CT scan
Mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy on CT scan
CT-guided biopsy of a pulmonary nodule demonstrated a malignant neoplasm
Tumor cells composed of spindle cells
Immunohistochemical staining positive for Bcl-2, vimentin, EMA, CD56, CD99, and TLE-1
Immunohistochemical staining negative for CD34, CD10, p63, cytokeratin, S100, desmin, and synaptophysin

raw.champion: Malignant solitary fibrous tumor of the spine
raw.rationale: The presence of a mixed sclerotic and lytic lesion in the T12 vertebral body, along with the malignant neoplasm composed of spindle cells and specific immunohistochemical staining patterns (positive for Bcl-2, vimentin, EMA, CD56, CD99, and TLE-1, and negative for others), supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: Typically has a different immunohistochemical profile, often positive for CD99 but usually negative for Bcl-2 and other markers found in this case.

rejected.label: Primitive neuroectodermal tumor
rejected.why: Usually presents with different clinical and radiological features and has distinct immunohistochemical characteristics.

rejected.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
rejected.why: While it shares some immunohistochemical features, the malignant behavior and specific location in the spine, along with metastatic disease, point more towards a malignant solitary fibrous tumor of the spine.

rejected.label: Hemangiopericytoma
rejected.why: Now considered a variant of solitary fibrous tumor/hemangiopericytoma, but the specific malignant behavior and spinal location with metastasis make malignant solitary fibrous tumor of the spine a more precise diagnosis.
